example.romaji: Kinou wa tasukete kurete arigatou ne.
example.ja: 昨日は助けてくれてありがとうね。
example.english: Thanks for helping me out yesterday.

examplePolite.romaji: Kinou wa tasukete itadaite, arigatou gozaimashita.
examplePolite.ja: 昨日は助けていただいて、ありがとうございました。
examplePolite.english: Thank you for helping me out yesterday.

notes: For help with a chore or task, tetsudau is more natural.

english: be a big help; be saved
use: Said as thanks: 'Tasukaru!' or 'Tasukatta!' means 'That really helps!'.

example.ja: 本当に助かったよ、ありがとう。
example.english: That was a huge help, thanks.

examplePolite.ja: 本当に助かりました、ありがとうございます。
examplePolite.english: That was a huge help, thank you.

notes: Pairs with tasukeru: tasukeru is what you do for someone, tasukaru is how it lands on you.

use: For rooting for a team, a friend's plans or a favourite idol; 'Ouen shiteru yo' means 'I'm behind you'.

example.ja: ずっと応援してるからね。
example.english: I'll always be rooting for you.

examplePolite.ja: ずっと応援しています。
examplePolite.english: I'll always be rooting for you.

notes: Mostly moral support; for practical help use tasukeru or tetsudau.

use: For chipping in on a shared job; the noun kyouryoku (cooperation) is common too.

example.romaji: Minna de kyouryoku shite ganbarou yo.
example.ja: みんなで協力して頑張ろうよ。
example.english: Let's all pull together and do our best.

examplePolite.ja: みんなで協力して頑張りましょう。
examplePolite.english: Let's all pull together and do our best.

notes: 'Gokyouryoku onegai shimasu' is the set request for cooperation in notices and announcements.

use: Hands-on backup at work or in a project; also customer support.

example.romaji: Nanika attara sapooto suru kara ne.
example.ja: 何かあったらサポートするからね。
example.english: If anything comes up, I'll back you up.

examplePolite.ja: 何かあったらサポートしますね。
examplePolite.english: If anything comes up, I'll back you up.

notes: Close to ouen, but sapooto is practical help and ouen is mostly cheering.

use: 'Makasete!' means 'Leave it to me!'; 'Makaseru yo' hands a decision to the other person.

examplePolite.romaji: Ryouri wa watashi ni makasete kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: 料理は私に任せてください。
examplePolite.english: Please leave the cooking to me.

notes: The person who takes the job gets ni: 'Kimi ni makaseru' means 'I'll leave it to you'.

english: leaving it to someone; chef's choice
use: Used as 'omakase suru' or 'omakase de' to hand over a choice; in restaurants, the chef's-choice menu.

example.english: I'll leave the colour up to you.

examplePolite.english: I'll leave the colour up to you.

notes: The polite face of makaseru; you use it about yourself handing over a choice.

english: rely on, depend on, count on
use: Often as 'Itsu demo tayotte ne' (you can always count on me).

example.ja: 困ったらいつでも頼ってね。
example.english: If you're ever stuck, you can always count on me.

examplePolite.romaji: Komattara itsu demo tayotte kudasai ne.
examplePolite.ja: 困ったらいつでも頼ってくださいね。
examplePolite.english: If you're ever stuck, you can always count on me.

notes: Don't mix up with tanomu (ask a favour); tayoru is leaning on someone.

use: 'Suki ni shite' can be a friendly 'go ahead' or an annoyed 'whatever, do what you want', depending on tone.

example.romaji: Ato wa suki ni shite ii yo.
example.ja: あとは好きにしていいよ。
example.english: After that, do whatever you like.

examplePolite.romaji: Ato wa suki ni shite ii desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: あとは好きにしていいですよ。
examplePolite.english: After that, feel free to do whatever you like.

notes: Said flatly in an argument, it sounds cold.

english: go out with, date; keep someone company
use: 'Tsukiatte kudasai' is the classic ask to be someone's partner; 'tsukiatteru' means they're dating.

example.ja: あの二人、付き合ってるらしいよ。
example.english: Apparently those two are going out.

examplePolite.romaji: Ano futari wa tsukiatte iru rashii desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: あの二人は付き合っているらしいですよ。
examplePolite.english: Apparently those two are going out.

notes: Second sense: come along with someone, as in 'Kaimono ni tsukiatte' (come shopping with me).

use: The person you split from takes to: 'Kare to wakareta' (I broke up with him).

example.english: I broke up with my girlfriend.

examplePolite.english: I broke up with my girlfriend.

notes: Wakareta (broke up) sounds close to wakatta (got it).

english: confess one's feelings, ask someone out
use: The big moment of telling someone you like them and asking to date.

example.romaji: Kinou, Yuki ni kokuhaku shita n da.
example.ja: 昨日、ユキに告白したんだ。
example.english: I told Yuki how I feel yesterday.

examplePolite.romaji: Kinou, Yuki-san ni kokuhaku shita n desu.
examplePolite.ja: 昨日、ユキさんに告白したんです。
examplePolite.english: I told Yuki how I feel yesterday.

notes: Slang kokuru is short for kokuhaku suru. It can also mean confessing a secret, but the romance sense dominates.

english: be popular romantically, get a lot of attention
use: Often as motesou (looks like they'd be popular) or motenai (gets no attention).

example.english: I bet he's really popular with girls.

examplePolite.romaji: Kare wa zettai motemasu yo ne.
examplePolite.ja: 彼は絶対モテますよね。
examplePolite.english: I bet he's really popular with girls.

use: 'Kekkon shite iru' means 'is married'; the partner takes to.

example.romaji: Ani ga raigetsu kekkon suru n da.
example.ja: 兄が来月結婚するんだ。
example.english: My brother's getting married next month.

examplePolite.romaji: Ani ga raigetsu kekkon suru n desu.
examplePolite.ja: 兄が来月結婚するんです。
examplePolite.english: My brother's getting married next month.

english: meet (for the first time), come across
use: For a first meeting, often a meaningful one.

example.romaji: Futari wa doko de deatta no?
example.ja: 二人はどこで出会ったの？

examplePolite.romaji: Futari wa doko de deatta n desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 二人はどこで出会ったんですか？

notes: Au is meeting up as planned; deau is meeting for the first time or by chance.

use: The ex-partner takes to: 'Kare to rikon shita'.

example.romaji: Ryoushin wa mukashi rikon shita n da.
example.ja: 両親は昔離婚したんだ。
example.english: My parents divorced a long time ago.

examplePolite.romaji: Ryoushin wa mukashi rikon shita n desu.
examplePolite.ja: 両親は昔離婚したんです。
examplePolite.english: My parents divorced a long time ago.

use: Mostly in the past, for how people first met.

example.romaji: Kanojo to wa shigoto de shiriatta n da.
example.ja: 彼女とは仕事で知り合ったんだ。

examplePolite.romaji: Kanojo to wa shigoto de shiriatta n desu.
examplePolite.ja: 彼女とは仕事で知り合ったんです。

notes: The noun shiriai means an acquaintance.

use: The person proposed to takes ni; 'puropoozu sareta' means 'got proposed to'.

example.ja: 昨日彼にプロポーズされた！

examplePolite.ja: 昨日彼にプロポーズされました。

notes: Only for marriage; a business proposal is teian.
